flagged.evidence: The text says that if “ψ(D^{n−1}_+)=\overline{e^{n−1}}” and the remaining boundary lies in the lower skeleton, then the inclusion is an elementary expansion; it does not require ψ|D^{n−1}_+ to be a characteristic map. For n=2, take \bar X=[0,1] with one open 1-cell e, map the upper semicircle by t↦sin²(2πt) onto [0,1], and map the lower semicircle constantly to 0. These satisfy the written conditions, but the attached 2-cell gives H₂(Y,\bar X)≅Z (there is no new 1-cell), so the inclusion is not a homotopy equivalence and cannot be an elementary expansion.

The first bullet requires only that φ|Q^{n−1} be a characteristic map. The dependency def-cell-attachment-by-a-characteristic-map defines this as the quotient map from D^n, whose boundary may identify points. For example, let X be a point, attach a loop e¹ at it, then attach e² with one boundary semicircle given by the characteristic map D¹→e¹∪X and the other mapped to X. The first bullet holds, but D¹→\overline{e¹}=S¹ is not a homeomorphism, contrary to the claimed equivalent condition.

The text says the new edge may join the new vertex “to itself.” A loop at the new vertex has both endpoints outside X, whereas the definition requires the remaining boundary value to lie in X. With X a point, adding a disjoint new vertex and loop adds an S¹ component, so the inclusion is not an elementary expansion.
